one_line: Three contradicted facts (two blocking) and a misattributed lab name require fixes before publish.

findings.quote: Meta's newest model matches GPT-4.1 Sol and you can test it today
findings.instruction: The verification block flags this as contradicted: the source says Artificial Analysis scores Muse Wonder (Max) as equivalent to GPT-6.1 Sol, not GPT-4.1 Sol. Rewrite the headline to name GPT-6.1 Sol, e.g. 'Meta's newest model matches GPT-6.1 Sol and you can test it today'.

findings.quote: Meta's Muse Wonder lands at GPT-4.1 Sol parity on Artificial Analysis scoring
findings.instruction: Contradicted by source: replace 'GPT-4.1 Sol' with 'GPT-6.1 Sol' to match the Artificial Analysis scoring cited in the verification block.

findings.quote: Muse 1.3 released just six weeks prior
findings.instruction: Contradicted by source: the source gives Muse 1.3's release date as September 2nd; from October 12 (Simon Willison's post date) that is approximately six weeks, but the verification flags it as contradicted. Verify the exact interval against the source and replace 'just six weeks prior' with the accurate elapsed time or the explicit date 'released September 2nd'.

findings.quote: Spotify's ad platform ships 70% AI-generated creative in production.
findings.instruction: The verification block flags this as unsupported: the source says 'more than 70% of ads currently are using AI tools', not that 70% of creative is AI-generated. 'AI-generated creative' overstates what the source claims. Rewrite to match the source, e.g. 'Spotify's ad platform now runs AI tools across more than 70% of ads in production.'

findings.quote: Meta's AI lab reaches the frontier just 14 months after founding
findings.instruction: The story body identifies the lab as MSL, not Meta's AI lab. Meta's AI lab (FAIR/Meta AI) is a long-established entity; MSL is a separate, newer lab. The headline incorrectly attributes MSL's achievement to Meta's AI lab. Rewrite to name MSL explicitly, e.g. 'MSL reaches the frontier just 14 months after founding'.

findings.quote: Practitioners benchmarking frontier models now have a fourth credible option, accessible via a single CLI plugin.
findings.instruction: This take's proposition ('a fourth credible option') repeats the same frame as the Big Picture take for c_aa2cdf2fdfaea403 ('MSL's Wonder Full makes it four'). Two takes in the same issue share the 'fourth credible vendor/option' scaffold. Rewrite this take to focus on the specific Hands-On angle — the CLI accessibility and benchmark parity — rather than the vendor-count frame already owned by the Big Picture story.

findings.quote: Does your agent governance cover actions taken outside your organisation's GitHub perimeter?
findings.instruction: The closing strategic question is well-anchored to a specific decision boundary (GitHub perimeter governance), which is in-voice for Big Picture. However, the question has a near-obvious answer for any reader who has followed the story — the answer is almost certainly 'no', making it rhetorical rather than genuinely strategic. Sharpen to a question that surfaces a real decision fork, e.g. 'Which team in your org owns agent permissions that extend beyond your GitHub organisation boundary?'

findings.quote: Watch the talk before your next agent architecture review; the boundary-enforcement patterns are directly portable.
findings.instruction: The Hands-On closing imperative names an action (watch the talk) but the artefact trigger is vague — 'your next agent architecture review' is not a specific artefact. Sharpen to name a concrete artefact and trigger, e.g. 'Before your next architecture review, map Spotify's compile-time visibility rules against your own inter-agent boundary enforcement and identify which boundaries currently have no owner.'

findings.quote: Tev-Gym supplies 1,170 verified environments and per-step reward shaping, lifting a 27-billion open model to 47.3 on the agentic benchmark.
findings.instruction: The sentence names 'the agentic benchmark' without specifying which benchmark (τ-bench), making it unverifiable for a reader who has not read the story. Replace 'the agentic benchmark' with 'the τ-bench agentic benchmark' to match the story body.

findings.quote: Today's practical stories each expose a gap between what a tool passes and what it actually delivers safely.
findings.instruction: The synthesis opens on a pattern claim that fits the security benchmark story well but sits awkwardly over the Spotify architecture story, which is about boundary enforcement and scale rather than a safety gap. The framing is slightly too narrow to cover all three stories. Revise the opening sentence to name the shared structural shape across all three — functional thresholds clearing while an adjacent harder requirement (security, boundary enforcement, or vendor parity) quietly lags — so the synthesis is genuinely section-anchored rather than story-anchored to one of the three.

findings.quote: Install it via the LLM CLI and run Muse Wonder at max reasoning level against your current frontier baseline before committing to a vendor.
findings.instruction: This story covers the same MSL/Meta Wonder Full frontier model as Big Picture story c_aa2cdf2fdfaea403, creating a split-coverage situation where the same model appears in two sections. The Hands-On angle (CLI plugin, benchmark parity test) is legitimate, but Arman should confirm the two stories are sufficiently differentiated in scope — the Big Picture story covers vendor-count implications while this covers the practitioner test path — and that readers will not experience them as duplicates.

findings.quote: On-device agentic inference defaulted to cloud offload; capable local agents now run on consumer hardware.
findings.instruction: The take's first clause ('defaulted to cloud offload') is a past-state setup rather than a present-tense declarative position. The operational test 'It is now the case that on-device agentic inference defaulted to cloud offload' does not parse cleanly. Rewrite as a single present-tense declarative, e.g. 'Capable local agents now run on consumer hardware, ending the default assumption that agentic inference requires cloud offload.'

note: verdict rule: blocking >= 1 (A blocking finding is reputational or liability exposure, or a factual claim the issue cannot stand behind. One is enough; there is no volume at which it becomes acceptable.) | 2 echo(es) not counted: the same defect filed again in another field or under another criterion
